raw_response:
I'm 65 now, and I've farmed these 15 mu in Quzhou for 40 years. Never went to school — can't read those extension pamphlets even if they gave them to me. I farm by watching, remembering, and talking to my neighbors. My old man works off‑farm at a construction site in Handan when he can find work, so most days it's just me out here. We're getting old, our backs aren't what they used to be, and we don't have much cash to throw around. Every yuan I spend on fertilizer is a yuan I don't have if someone gets sick.

I keep 5 mu in garlic because it brings good money at the market, though it's back‑breaking work. The other 10 mu I put in wheat last fall, same as always. After wheat harvest in early June, I'll plant maize on that same 10 mu. That's my system — garlic on one piece, wheat‑maize double crop on the rest.

**Wheat (10 mu):** The wheat went in last October with seed I saved from the year before. Come March when it greens up, I'll spread about half a big bag of urea on each mu — I don't weigh it, I just know the scoop. That's what I've done for 20 years. If it looks a bit yellow at jointing, maybe I'll add a little more, but urea got expensive and I need to save cash for maize seed. I'll irrigate twice if the sky doesn't give us rain — once when it turns green, once at jointing. I won't water at flowering unless it's terribly dry; the electricity for the pump is too dear. I'll spray for weeds once in early spring. If I see aphids, I'll get medicine from the village shop. Last year I got about 800 jin per mu, this year I expect about the same, maybe 850 jin if the weather smiles on us.

**Garlic (5 mu):** I planted it last October with cloves I saved. Garlic needs a lot of fussing — weeding, checking, worrying. In March I'll put down some fertilizer, maybe a scoop of compound and a bit of urea per mu. Old Wang down the road used more fertilizer on his garlic last year and his bulbs were big, so I'm thinking of adding a little extra, but then I look at my pocket and think twice. I'll water it twice in spring. You can't water too much before harvest or the bulbs rot in the ground. I need to watch for rust — if I see those orange spots, I'll spray fungicide quick. I'm hoping for about 1,400 jin per mu. Last year was 1,300 jin, so maybe a bit better if I don't get lazy with the weeding.

**Maize (10 mu):** After the wheat comes off in early June, I have to move fast — sometimes the window is less than a week. I'll hire the machine to rotary‑till and plant if I can find one; costs about 30–40 yuan per mu but it's fast, and at my age I can't bend over planting by hand on 10 mu anymore. I buy hybrid seed from the shop, about 3 jin per mu. At planting I'll put compound fertilizer in the furrow — roughly one bag per mu. Then when the maize is knee‑high, I'll topdress with urea. If the summer rains come steady, I might only irrigate once. Usually I end up irrigating twice. I'll spray herbicide when I plant, and if there are armyworms later, I'll spray insecticide. I expect about 900 jin per mu.

Money is always tight. I have about 4,500 yuan I can spend on inputs this season. The wheat topdressing and garlic fertilizer will take a chunk, and maize seed and fertilizer will take the biggest bite. I'd rather apply a bit too much fertilizer than too little — a bad year hurts more than a good year helps, and at my age I can't afford to lose money on a crop failure.
